scope: Current CPU-only / explicit GPU+CPU Backend cold configuration through real Graph/Compute/provider execution; source only. No default change, build, GPU, benchmark, runtime test or network.

conclusions.fact: Backend::create(selection,budgets,DefaultContextOptions) forwards the original same options to both CPU-primary and explicit CPU-assist endpoints. Model accepts Backend&&, so an owner can configure either mode without a second executor/runtime or Model API. No lost-field or unavailable lower-level binding was found.

Qwen create_execution and its delegating Model constructors still call the default two-argument Backend factory. Current CLI exposes backend and cpu-ffn-layers, not CPU thread/executor configuration. Their selected ggml programs retain native_threads=1 and empty borrowed executor. This is a real facility-consumption opportunity, not a blocking foundation/CLI feature gap: explicit prepared-Backend Model construction already exists.

With those defaults ggml internal programs have one-thread native budget; native fallback work chooses one task from empty executor concurrency1; oneDNN threadpool/fanout also receives the empty executor. Supplying executor concurrency alone does not parallelize a ggml program: its entire execution is submitted as one executor task. native_threads and executor are independent policies.

ATen low-precision/general alternatives use an independent shared CPU runtime, controlled only by explicit startup configure_runtime_threads. Default native_threads=1 does not clamp ATen, OpenMP, BLAS, simultaneous callers or all process threads. No actual selected whole-Model provider mix or runtime thread count was measured.

CPU-assist uses the same conservative1/empty defaults. These avoid automatically multiplying private pools while the GPU and host-submit path exist, but optimal hybrid threading is unmeasured. No source evidence establishes that1 is optimal or that larger counts are a gain; pure CPU and mixed workloads should remain separately selected owner policies.

anchors.fact: Optional cold CPU options are checked before endpoint creation, never implicitly create CPU; same initialize_cpu for primary and assist.
Natural factory uses original defaults; explicit Backend&& Model seam preserves a caller-configured endpoint and validates CPU placement.

Actual CPU or mixed Model compilation requires finite known workspace-domain budgets. A configured Backend created with default-unlimited budgets is valid for the old tiny Graph case but is not sufficient for a real Model.
Borrowed allocator/executor; independent ggml native thread budget; global ATen runtime is a different explicit startup API.
Graph forwards options.executor/native_threads into original ggml region provider, oneDNN and native fallback.
Direct and Graph share original provider assembly; native_threads and executor concurrency also qualify original one-thread route preferences.
Each Invocation builds CpuExecution with configured native_threads; executor.parallel_for(1) wraps a complete program. Invalid native budget is rejected in ggml context.

Cold persistent native threadpool and workspace per Invocation; polling0; replay runs original program; reset frees its pool. More threads may multiply worker/pool resources across prepared invocations, not share a global quota.
Empty borrowed executor is caller-thread synchronous loop with concurrency1; no implicit worker creation.
Native fanout is bounded by executor concurrency, independent units and minimum work; no executor means one task.
Prepared native synchronous fanout; detectable nested execution stays caller-thread to preserve progress.
oneDNN threadpool reports executor concurrency and delegates synchronous fanout; BRGEMM uses same original executor path.
Prepared BRGEMM task fanout uses ParallelExecutorRef.
Separate shared ATen intra-op startup setting; no per-Context restore or automatic change. Foreign runtime use and configured limits must be coordinated.

Actual capability admission and original route preference still apply. Thread/executor settings can disable specific qualified one-thread policies; a future cost comparison must record actual routes, not assume only scheduling differs.

Existing actual package consumer adapts application-owned hyle::sched::Scheduler/bulk_execute to synchronous ParallelExecutorRef and handles nested progress; reuse this shape if an owner wants library scheduler workers.

smallest_next_step.candidate: If CPU facility performance is selected next, use the existing explicit Backend factory and Model(Backend&&...) seam in a bounded real cached CPU consumer, with declared native_threads and/or existing Scheduler adapter. Report exact providers, requested native budget, executor concurrency and independent ATen limits. No new thread pool, option registry, global setter-on-construction or default auto-core policy is required.
smallest_next_step.hybrid: Select a separate explicit CPU-assist policy; do not infer it from CPU-only tuning or scale every prepared Invocation to all cores. No experiment is launched by this memo.
smallest_next_step.required_actual_model_fact: The caller must supply the same finite WorkspaceBudgets/placement as create_execution, not Backend::create(selection,{},options): record_execution_plan rejects unlimited CPU or mixed domains. If avoiding repeated admission arithmetic becomes necessary, forward the original cold options through create_execution while leaving its existing finite-budget calculation unchanged; that is small consumer glue, not a missing executor or new budget owner.

evidence_boundary.read_only_interpretation: Existing proof exercised configured/default tiny CPU Graph, a borrowed dispatch probe, move and rejection semantics at native_threads1. It did not establish parallel speed, native_threads>1, whole real Model configured options, mixed endpoint throughput or process-wide bounds; not repeated here. Its default-unlimited Backend budget is a Graph-only fixture choice; do not reuse it unchanged for real Model admission.
evidence_boundary.package_executor_sample: Source consumer inspected only; no new execution result claimed.

not_checked: No CPU/GPU throughput, selected real-model route census, NUMA/affinity, core-count tuning, total live native worker count or memory overhead measured.
No new broad provider audit or CMake/hardware matrix; no conclusion that all parallel facilities are idle or that default1 is slow.
